user_goal: Record and verify the actual TCP listener process while safely migrating legacy venv-wrapper owner records, then publish and attest the patch.

baseline.protection_evidence: origin/main and immutable v0.1.11 release resolve to the reviewed commit
baseline.selection_reason: Live upgrade proved the venv launcher PID differs from the child process that owns the TCP listener.

semantic_changes: Persist the actual listening child PID and its exact identity after bind.

Accept a legacy wrapper record only when the current listener is its direct child and command line, creation instant, root, connector, port, host, wrapper executable, and hashes prove the same owned launch.
Preserve foreign/stale/PID-reused failure and publish v0.1.12.
No ownership inference from HTML or loose argv substrings, unrelated behavior, foreign takeover, secret exposure, tag rewrite, or unreviewed release.

invariants: New records identify the process that owns the configured listening socket.
Legacy wrapper migration requires direct parent-child lineage plus every recorded identity field that remains applicable.
PID, port, host, root, connector, executable lineage, creation identity, and command hash remain required.
Foreign and malformed listeners survive unchanged.
PR, CodeRabbit, CI, receipts, public main, tag, package, and live service bind one exact candidate.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: New startup records the actual listening PID and later owned restart recognizes it.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Wrapper PID persisted as socket owner.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: The exact legacy wrapper-to-direct-child listener relationship is accepted once.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Unrelated child or foreign process accepted.

acceptance_cases.promised_behavior: PR 6 review and exact-head CI are green.
Signed chain, verifier, and guard approve exact v0.1.12.
Untouched legacy listener upgrades to exact healthy v0.1.12 and a second install recognizes the new owner record.
acceptance_cases.forbidden_behavior: Manual PID stop or dirty/unhealthy install.

proof_requirements.claim: Real process-boundary proof records socket owner and supports a second restart.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: two consecutive installs and PID assertions
proof_requirements.expected_observation: record PID equals TCP owner each time

proof_requirements.claim: Legacy migration accepts only exact direct-child identity and rejects altered lineage/fields.
Raw review and exact-head checks are green.
Independent signed chain passes verifier and guard.
Public and twice-installed artifacts are exact, healthy, owned, and clean.
proof_requirements.command_or_read_only_check: Actions, release, two installs, owner, health, git

release_requirements.required_receipt: signed chain accepted by verifier and guard

stop_conditions: Unexpected diff, loose parent-child acceptance, foreign listener termination, dirty/multiple worktrees, failed tests/review/CI, non-PASS receipt, verifier/guard rejection, or live failure.
known_discrepancies: v0.1.11 package installed but restart failed closed because the legacy record names venv wrapper PID 26296 while TCP port 53327 is owned by its direct child PID 18052; both share exact command line and creation lineage and the original listener remains healthy.

requirement_trace.authority: User continuation through a working reviewed release
